metadata.consistency_ledger:
TRANSLITERATION: not needed — names stay as written. (Sarah, James, Anna, Davies, Jones, Manchester, London, France = Frankreich, Africa is not in this pod's script — all personal names and surnames stay exactly as in canon.)

PRICES — notional conversion to Euro at realistic current Austrian café/taxi levels, Cent voiced, strictly monotonic:
- "eight pound forty" (Scene 7, four coffees + one pastry + water) → **"neunzehn Euro achtzig"** (€19.80), spoken exactly so: "des mocht neunzehn Euro achtzig zsammen."
- "twelve pound fifty" (Scene 14, ~20-min taxi ride) → **"vierundzwanzig Euro fünfzig"** (€24.50): "des mocht vierundzwanzig Euro fünfzig."
No other money figures occur. Never render pounds/pence; no other amounts may reuse these figures.

TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME: **Deitsch** — everywhere the canon says "Austrian German" (lines 23, 84, 85, 131, 136 ×2), exactly as the course itself renders it ("i red iatz a bissl Deitsch"). A young Grazer never says "österreichisches Deutsch" in conversation; the bare course word "Deitsch" is the pin.

RECURRING LINES — one rendering, verbatim wherever the canonical line recurs:
- "Good morning" (Sc 1×2, 7, 10, 12) = **"Guten Morgen"**
- "Good afternoon" (Sc 3×2, 11) = **"Grüß Gott"** (Austria has no spoken "guten Nachmittag")
- "Good evening" (Sc 4, 5, 8, 9) = **"guten Abend"**
- "Hello" informal (Sc 4, 6) = **"Servus"**; "Hello" to taxi driver (Sc 14) = **"Grüß Gott"**
- "What can I get you?" (Sc 3, 7, 8) = **"Wos darf's sein?"**
- "I'd like …, please" (Sc 3, 7, 8, 9) = **"i mechat …, bitte"** (never "i hätte gern")
- "Can/Could I have …?" (Sc 7, 8, 12) = **"kann i … hobn, bitte?"**
- "Could I pay by card?" (Sc 7 l.38, Sc 14 l.128) = **"Kann i mit Karte zahlen?"** — identical both times
- "Yes, of course" (Sc 6, 8, 12, 14) = **"jo, klar"**; bare "Of course" (Sc 7, 9, 11) = **"klar"**
- "Thank you very much" (Sc 3, 10, 13) = **"dankschen"**; plain "Thank you" = **"danke"**
- "Goodbye" (Sc 3, 10) = **"Wiederschaun!"**
- "See you later / then / tomorrow" (Sc 1, 4, 5) = **"bis später" / "bis dann" / "bis morgen"**
- "Excuse me" (Sc 2, 6, 9, 10, 13) = **"Entschuldigung"**
- "You've been very helpful" (Sc 10 l.83, Sc 13 l.119) = **"Sie hobn ma sehr gholfn."** — identical both times
- "booking under the name X" (Sc 9, 11) = **"a Reservierung auf den Namen X"** ("mir hobn" / "i hob")
- wine list (Sc 8 l.48, Sc 9 l.70) = **"de Weinkarte"**: "Kann i de Weinkarte sehn?" / "Kennan wir de Weinkarte sehn?"
- "at the moment" (Sc 4, 14) = **"grod"**; "I'm sorry" (Sc 4, 6) = **"tut ma leid"**; "I'm not sure …" (Sc 8, 15) = **"i bin ma ned sicher, …"**; "a little / a bit" (Sc 6, 15) = **"a bissl"** (never + "Zeit"); "on holiday" (Sc 6, 10) = **"auf Urlaub"** (never "im Urlaub")
- "to take away" (Sc 3, 7) = **"zum mitnehmen"** (lowercase per native check); sit-in = **"zum do trinken"**
- Lexical pins: water = **Wossa**; glass = **Glaserl** (course-licensed, all glass sizes); coffee = **Kaffee** ("an Kaffee"); black coffee = **a Schwarzer**; white coffee = **a Brauner**; Americano = **a Verlängerter**; card reader (Sc 7 l.39, Sc 14 l.129) = **"des Gerät"**; cashpoint (Sc 13) = **"a Bankomat"**; pub food scene venue words follow the course pin (Gasthaus, not Beisl/Wirtshaus/Kneipe)
- NARRATOR counting lines (every scene): numbers — **oans, zwoa, drei**, then standard spellings (vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, fünfzehn, … hundert, tausend, hunderttausend); colours — **weiß, schwarz, rot, grün, blau, gelb, orange, lila, rosa, grau** (purple = lila, pink = rosa); days — **Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag** (never Sonnabend); times — **zwölf Uhr, ein Uhr, elf Uhr**. Same spelling in every narrator line.

REGISTER: Customer–staff, both directions (barista, bartender, waiter, receptionist, pharmacist, shop assistant, taxi driver, and their customers) = **Sie**, in the course's native-checked treatment: Sie-grammar stays near-standard but keeps Graz vocabulary and the clitic **"S'"** ("Hobn S' …?", "wos brauchen S'?"). Transactional strangers (train passenger Sc 2, local giving directions Sc 13) = **Sie**. Friends and known neighbours (Sc 1, 4, 5, 15) = **du** at full Graz depth (i/mi/di, ned, wos, hob, mechat, wennst). Scene 6 (James/Anna, young peers socialising) = **du** from the first line. No pair ever switches level mid-scene.

SPEAKER GENDER: not marked in Austrian German — skip. (One consequential exception to carry anyway: Anna's "I'm a nurse" must use the female form **Krankenschwester** in both lines 22 and 24, since profession nouns are gendered; Anna is a woman, James a man, for any similar self-reference.)

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Wia oft soll i des Paracetamol nehmen?
sentences.known_text: How often should I take the paracetamol?

sentences.speaker: Pharmacist
sentences.target_text: Ane olle vier bis sechs Stunden, ned mehr als acht am Tog.
sentences.known_text: One every four to six hours, no more than eight a day.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Kann i de mit'm Essen nehmen?
sentences.known_text: Can I take them with food?

sentences.speaker: Pharmacist
sentences.target_text: Jo, mit'm Essen oder noch'm Essen is am besten.
sentences.known_text: Yes, with food or after food is best.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Danke. Kann i auch a Packerl Pflaster hobn, bitte?
sentences.known_text: Thank you. Could I also have a packet of plasters, please?

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: neunzehn. zwanzig. einundzwanzig. Mittwoch. Donnerstag.
sentences.known_text: nineteen. twenty. twenty-one. Wednesday. Thursday.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Entschuldigung, wissen S', wia i zum nächsten Supermarkt kumm?
sentences.known_text: Excuse me, do you know how I get to the nearest supermarket?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Jo, des san zirka zehn Minuten zu Fuß. Gehn S' geradeaus die Straßn do entlang.
sentences.known_text: Yes, it's about ten minutes on foot. Go straight along this road.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Bei da Kirchn do vorbei?
sentences.known_text: Past that church?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Jo, bei da Kirchn und bei da Post vorbei.
sentences.known_text: Yes, past the church and the post office.

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Beim zweiten Kreisverkehr nehmen S' die erste Ausfahrt.
sentences.known_text: At the second roundabout, take the first exit.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Und dann?
sentences.known_text: And then?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Sie sehn den Supermarkt auf Ihrer linken Seiten, direkt gegenüber von der Bushaltestelle.
sentences.known_text: You'll see the supermarket on your left, directly opposite the bus stop.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Wunderbar. Und gibt's do in der Nähe an Bankomat?
sentences.known_text: Wonderful. And is there a cashpoint nearby?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Jo, do gibt's oan in der Hauptstraßn, neben der Bäckerei.
sentences.known_text: Yes, there's one on the high street, next to the bakery.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Dankschen. Sie hobn ma sehr gholfn.
sentences.known_text: Thank you very much. You've helped me a lot.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: dreißig. vierzig. fünfzig. Freitag. Samstag.
sentences.known_text: thirty. forty. fifty. Friday. Saturday.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Grüß Gott. Können S' mi zum Bahnhof bringen, bitte?
sentences.known_text: Hello. Can you take me to the train station, please?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Jo, klar. Des kann a bissl dauern, es is grod viel Verkehr.
sentences.known_text: Yes, of course. It may take a bit, there's a lot of traffic at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Wos glauben S', wia long des ungefähr dauert?
sentences.known_text: About how long do you think it will take?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Vielleicht so zwanzig Minuten, wenn mir mit de Ampeln koa Pech hobn.
sentences.known_text: Perhaps about twenty minutes, if we don't have bad luck with the traffic lights.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Wissen S', wo i im Bahnhof a Ticket kriegen kann?
sentences.known_text: Do you know where I can get a ticket in the station?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Jo, i setz Sie direkt beim Ticketschalter ab.
sentences.known_text: Yes, I'll drop you off right by the ticket office.

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: So, do san ma. Des mocht vierundzwanzig Euro fünfzig.
sentences.known_text: Here we are. That's twenty-four euros fifty.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Kann i mit Karte zahlen?
sentences.known_text: Could I pay by card?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Jo, klar. Des Gerät is direkt do.
sentences.known_text: Yes, of course. The machine is right here.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: hundert. zweihundert. tausend. Sonntag. zwölf Uhr.
sentences.known_text: one hundred. two hundred. one thousand. Sunday. twelve o'clock.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Mocht's da wos aus, wenn i versuch, mit dir Deitsch reden zum üben? I lern no ned long, und i bin no a bissl nervös, wenn i mit andere Leut red.
sentences.known_text: Would you mind if I try to practise speaking Austrian German with you? I haven't been learning for very long yet, and I'm still a little nervous when I speak with other people.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Klar, koa Problem. Du redst es echt guat, kummt ma vor. I kann di leicht verstehn.
sentences.known_text: Of course, no problem. You seem to speak it very well. I can understand you easily.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Danke, des is guat zum wissen. I muass no mehr Wörter lernen, und i muass des zuhörn üben. I versteh de Leut ned guat, wenn s' ned langsam reden.
sentences.known_text: Thank you, that's good to know. I need to learn more words, and I need to practise listening. I don't understand people very well when they don't speak slowly.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Red i iatz langsam gnua für di?
sentences.known_text: Am I speaking slowly enough for you now?

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Jo, danke. Es is leichter, nur mit oana Person zum reden. Oba es is a bissl schwer, dass ma wos zum sogn einfällt. I bin ma ned sicher, wos i sogn soll, oba i fühl mi so, als ob i gnua reden kann, dass i anfangen kann, Gespräche zum hobn.
sentences.known_text: Yes, thank you. It's easier talking to just one person. But it's a bit difficult to think of something to say. I'm not sure what to say, but I feel as if I can speak enough to be able to start having conversations.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: I glaub, du mochst des echt guat. I bin beeindruckt. I glaub, du bist so weit, dass du anfangen kannst, mit jedn Deitsch zum reden, der wos Deitsch redt.
sentences.known_text: I think you're doing very well. I'm impressed. I think you're ready to start speaking Austrian German with anyone who speaks Austrian German.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Es is hoit a bissl frustrierend, wenn i ned schnell gnua denken kann, dass i mi richtig ausdrücken kann. Oba i woaß, dass i weiter üben muass, wenn i selbstbewusster reden wü.
sentences.known_text: It's just a little frustrating when I can't think quickly enough to express myself properly. But I know that I need to keep practising if I want to speak more confidently.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Du solltst scho selbstbewusst sein. I glaub, du mochst des viel besser, als wia du glaubst. I fühl mi wohl, wenn i mit dir red, und i red ned sehr langsam.
sentences.known_text: You should be confident already. I think you're doing much better than you realise. I feel comfortable speaking with you, and I'm not talking very slowly.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Des is genau de Übung, de wos i brauch. I glaub, i kann spürn, wia's mein Gehirn verändert, während mir reden! I bin da echt dankbar für deine Hilfe. Oba es is überraschend, wia müd i werd, wenn i in a Sproch red, de wos i ned so guat red.
sentences.known_text: This is exactly the practice I need. I think I can feel it changing my brain while we're talking! I'm really grateful for your help. But it's surprising how tired I get when I'm talking in a language I don't speak very well.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: I glaub, des is normal. Es is schwer, a neiche Sproch zum lernen. Oba es mocht so viel Spaß, wennst anfangst, Gespräche zum hobn, oder?
sentences.known_text: I think that's normal. Learning a new language is difficult. But it's so much fun when you start to have conversations, isn't it?

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Des stimmt echt. I bin echt froh, dass i scho so a langes Gespräch hobn kann. Und i hoff, dass mir in Zukunft no mehr Gespräche hobn kennan, während i immer besser werd.
sentences.known_text: It really is. I'm really happy that I can already have this long a conversation. And I hope we'll be able to have more conversations in the future as I keep getting better.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: hunderttausend. sechzig. siebzig. ein Uhr. elf Uhr.
sentences.known_text: a hundred thousand. sixty. seventy. one o'clock. eleven o'clock.
